git add internal/entiredb go.mod go.sum .golangci.yaml && git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
Vendor entiredb's entire-repo plugin into internal/entiredb/

Snapshot the kubectl-style entire-repo plugin tree from entiredb's
main branch (cmd/entire-repo + internal/cli{auth,api,dial,docs,cobra}
+ supporting client/auth/url machinery) under internal/entiredb/, so
the cli can ship a `repo` subcommand without execing a separate
binary. Open-source posture is preserved: only client-side and wire
contract code crosses the boundary; no entiredb server internals
come along.

This is the right surface — earlier work on this branch had vendored
cmd/entiredb/cli (the standalone-binary surface, requires
ENTIRE_BASE_URL to be set explicitly per command). The actually-in-
use surface is cmd/entire-repo, which:

  - Routes data-plane verbs via the cluster in the positional
    (<cluster>/et/<org>/<repo>) rather than a global env var.
  - Routes lifecycle verbs (create, delete, list, grant) through
    entire-core, no cluster URL required.
  - Reads auth from ~/.config/entire/contexts.json (written by
    `entire-core auth login`) rather than a parallel keyring slot.

Vendor directory layout mirrors upstream so refresh-from-upstream
is a directory-tree rsync rather than a manual diff. The one
exception is internal/gogitzlib, lifted to internal/entiredb/
gogitzlib so cmd/entire/main.go can blank-import it for the
klauspost zlib provider registration (Go's internal/ visibility
rule blocks the double-nested path).

Trims relative to upstream:

  - client/client.go has the admin gRPC surface stripped (Connect /
    ConnectWithAuth / ConnectWithRefresh + the admin field + the
    ~20 AdminFoo methods + adminpb import). Eliminates the
    gen/proto/publicapi/admin/v1 dependency entirely. The repo
    plugin uses ConnectRepoWithAuth / ConnectRepoWithRefresh
    (HTTP, not gRPC), so the admin surface is dead code here.
  - cliauth/creds.go ConnectWithOpsToken and ConnectToNodeWithOpsToken
    drop with their underlying admin Connect helpers; the rest of
    the admin token-resolution surface stays for binary refresh
    cleanliness even though it's unused in our reduced setup.
  - core/api copies only client.go (the api.Client wrapper).
  - httputil copies only cloudflare.go and oauth.go (the two files
    the vendored client.go actually consumes).
  - tlscert copies only tlscert.go (drops the server-side cert
    plumbing that pulls in entire.io/slogutil).
  - slogutil copies only log.go, slogctx.go, interpolation.go,
    stdout_handler.go (skips memberlist / zap bridge / attr-utils).

New module deps added by go mod tidy:
  - google.golang.org/grpc (auth interceptors + tlscert helper)
  - github.com/caarlos0/env/v11 (cliauth Config parsing)
  - github.com/gofrs/flock (contexts.json locking)
  - github.com/go-jose/go-jose/v4 (clilogin JWT verify)
  - github.com/cpuguy83/go-md2man/v2 (cobra/doc, used by clidocs)
  - github.com/lmittmann/tint (slogutil stdout handler)
  - github.com/oklog/ulid/v2 (core/model IDs)

Lint exclusions in .golangci.yaml scope the cli's stricter house
style off the vendored tree — it tracks upstream and is refreshed
in batches; holding it to cli's rules would make each refresh a
chain of style fix-ups that drift from upstream.

EOF

Bridge entire login into entiredb's contexts.json

After a successful `entire login` device flow, decode the JWT claims
and additionally write the entiredb-format credential store so
`entire repo` (and any future vendored entire-repo subcommand) picks
up the bearer without a separate `entire-core auth login` call.

Specifically, the bridge:

  - Stores the access token in the OS keyring under the
    `entire-core:<iss>` service slot (the keychain layout that the
    vendored cliauth + auth-interceptor expect).
  - Upserts a kubectl-style entry into ~/.config/entire/contexts.json
    (the file the vendored cliauth reads) carrying issuer URL,
    principal handle, and keychain-service name; flips current_context
    to it.

The token's iss and handle come from the JWT's own claims, already
validated at runLogin's validateReceivedToken step. Opaque (non-JWT)
tokens or claims missing iss/handle skip the bridge with a note —
the cli's own keyring write above is unconditional, so non-entiredb
surfaces (auth status / list / revoke) are unaffected.

Refresh tokens are not bridged: the device flow this CLI uses returns
only a bearer. The vendored auth-interceptor's refresh path already
logs a warning and falls back to the existing bearer on expiry,
matching the cli's pre-existing single-token auth UX.

Failure to write the entiredb context is non-fatal — `entire login`
prints a warning and still succeeds. The cli's own keyring entry is
already persisted by the time the bridge runs, and we'd rather
report a partial success than fail an otherwise-good login.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF

The error's from the new plugin's positional parser — that's the design, not a regression from our work. The format is `<cluster>/<surface>/<org>/<repo>` where cluster is the data-cluster host (separate from auth host):

```
entire repo ls <cluster>/gh/entireio/cli   # GitHub mirror
entire repo ls <cluster>/et/<org>/<repo>   # native
entire repo ls entire://<cluster>/<surface>/<org>/<repo>   # pasted clone URL form
```

`gh/entireio/cli` got parsed as `cluster=gh`, `path=entireio/cli` — hence the surface-prefix complaint about `entireio/cli`.

You need the data-cluster host. From `entire auth status` you're logged in via `us.auth.entire.io` (auth), so your data cluster is probably `us.entire.io` or similar. Quickest way to find out:

```sh
entire repo list                    # shows repos you have access to
```

Each entry should carry a cluster host. Or your coworker can tell you what they use — for the EU example they showed, it'd be e.g. `eu.entire.io/gh/entireio/cli` or whatever the EU cluster is named.

If the cluster-discovery UX is rough, that's a real complaint we should bring to whoever owns the entiredb CLI — but it's the upstream design, not something our vendor introduced. Want me to dig deeper or is this enough to get you unstuck?

Here's the surface of each:

## entiredb's kubectl-style plugins on main

| Plugin | LOC | Subcommands | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| **`entire-repo`** (already vendored) | 2,157 | `clone`, `ls`, `log`, `files`, `diff`, `compare`, `branches`, `tags`, `merge` (`+--dry-run`), `rebase` (`+--dry-run`), `revert` (`+--dry-run`), `get-file`, `merge-base`, `create`, `delete`, `list`, `mirror`, `docs` | All user-facing repo verbs: lifecycle (create/delete/list against entire-core), content/data-plane (clone/log/merge/... against cluster), GitHub-mirror placement |
| **`entire-org`** | 114 | `create <name>`, `list`, `docs` | Org CRUD — both verbs hit entire-core, no cluster needed |
| **`entire-project`** | 198 | `create <name>`, `list [<org>]`, `docs` | Project CRUD — same model, entire-core only |
| **`entire-grant`** | 520 | `repo {add,remove,list}`, `project {add,remove,list}`, `org {add,remove,list}` (each with `--handle`, `--role`) | Membership / access grants across all three layers, entire-core only |

All four read auth from the same `~/.config/entire/contexts.json` that `entire login` now populates (after the bridge we just landed), so they'd all "just work" with one login.

## What it'd take to vendor the other three

They're much smaller than `entire-repo` and share the same shared-package set already vendored (`cliauth`, `cliapi`, `cliauth`, `clidocs`, `client/*`). Adding `entire-org`, `entire-project`, `entire-grant` is mostly:

1. Copy 4 dirs (~830 LOC total: 2 files for org, 2 for project, 5 for grant + the main.go shims)
2. Rewrite imports — same as before, one `sed` pass
3. Three thin wrappers in `cmd/entire/cli/` (one per plugin) — each ~20 lines, identical shape to `repo.go`
4. Add three labs entries

No new transitive deps; no surgery needed. The org/project/grant plugins are lifecycle-only (entire-core HTTP, no gRPC, no scoped JWT exchange), so they're simpler than `entire-repo`.

Want me to vendor them in the same branch?

23		// Create context that cancels on interrupt
24		ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
25

27		sigChan := make(chan os.Signal, 1)
28		signals := []os.Signal{os.Interrupt}
29		if runtime.GOOS != "windows" {

42		// dispatcher: prepend the managed bin dir to PATH before resolution.
43		// Idempotent and silent on failure (managed installs simply won't be
44		// found this run; PATH-installed plugins still work). The closure
45		// restores PATH so built-in commands and their subprocesses don't
46		// inherit the prepended dir. When a plugin runs, we skip the restore
47		// — the os.Exit ends the process, and the plugin child intentionally
48		// inherits the prepended PATH so it can spawn sibling managed plugins.
49		restorePATH := cli.PrependPluginBinDirToPATH(ctx)

52			cancel()

input.command:
gh pr create --draft --title "Vendor entiredb repo/org/project/grant plugins into the cli" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Summary

Vendor the kubectl-style plugin tree from entiredb's `main` (`cmd/entire-{repo,org,project,grant}` + the `internal/{cliauth,cliapi,clidial,clidocs,clicobra}` shared infrastructure) into `internal/entiredb/`, and wire each plugin as a hidden top-level subcommand under `entire labs`. After `entire login`, the full kubectl-style surface works without `entire-core` or the separate plugin binaries installed.

This replaces a previous attempt on this branch that had vendored the legacy `cmd/entiredb/cli` surface — that one required `ENTIRE_BASE_URL` to be set per command and had a manual auth bridge. The cutover-branch plugin tree (now on entiredb's main) is the right surface: lifecycle verbs go through entire-core, data-plane verbs carry the cluster in the positional, and auth is uniformly `contexts.json`.

## Layout

| Cli command | Vendored from | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `entire repo` | `entiredb/cmd/entire-repo` | clone, log, files, diff, compare, branches, tags, merge/rebase/revert (`+--dry-run` each), get-file, merge-base, ls, create, delete, list, mirror, docs |
| `entire org` | `entiredb/cmd/entire-org` | `create <name>`, `list` |
| `entire project` | `entiredb/cmd/entire-project` | `create <name>`, `list [<org>]` |
| `entire grant` | `entiredb/cmd/entire-grant` | `{repo,project,org} {add,remove,list}` with `--handle` / `--role` |

All four are `Hidden: true` and listed in `entire labs`. Display names + Long strings + Example blocks are rebranded from the upstream `entire-<x>` form to `entire <x>` so help / docs / errors read consistently.

## Auth

`entire login` now does what it always did (writes a bare access token to the `entire-cli` keyring slot) **plus** decodes the JWT and mirrors it into the entiredb-format credential store:

  - Writes the access token at `entire-core:<iss>` (the keychain layout the vendored cliauth + auth-interceptor expect).
  - Upserts a kubectl-style entry into `~/.config/entire/contexts.json` (issuer URL, principal handle, keychain service); flips `current_context` to it.

That replaces the separate `entire-core auth login` step the entiredb plugins used to require. Refresh tokens aren't bridged because the device flow this CLI uses doesn't issue them — same behavior the cli has always had.

## UX polish

- Examples + Long strings rewritten from \`entire-<x>\` (upstream kubectl-style binary name) to \`entire <x>\` (the dispatched form users actually type).
- Arg-count errors (\`accepts 1 arg(s), received 0\`) now print the failing subcommand's usage block before the error, matching how unknown-command / unknown-flag already worked.
- Vendored sources held to their own house style via a \`.golangci.yaml\` exclusion (cli's stricter defaults would make each upstream refresh a chain of style fix-ups).

## Trims relative to upstream

- \`client/client.go\` admin gRPC surface stripped (Connect / ConnectWithAuth / ConnectWithRefresh + admin field + ~20 AdminFoo methods + adminpb import). The plugins use \`ConnectRepoWithAuth\` / \`ConnectRepoWithRefresh\` (HTTP), so the admin surface is dead code here. Saves ~5.8K LOC of admin proto stubs.
- \`cliauth/creds.go\` ConnectWithOpsToken / ConnectToNodeWithOpsToken stripped (only the admin gRPC sites called these). Other admin token-resolution helpers stay for upstream-refresh cleanliness.
- \`core/api\` copies only \`client.go\` (the api.Client wrapper), not the 30-file server-side admin surface.
- \`httputil\` copies only \`cloudflare.go\` and \`oauth.go\`.
- \`tlscert\` copies only \`tlscert.go\` (drops the server-side cert plumbing that pulls in slogutil).
- \`slogutil\` copies only \`log.go\` / \`slogctx.go\` / \`interpolation.go\` / \`stdout_handler.go\`.
- Five auth-error message strings rewritten from \`entire-core auth login\` to \`entire login\` (the cli's actual command).

## New module deps

\`google.golang.org/grpc\`, \`github.com/caarlos0/env/v11\`, \`github.com/gofrs/flock\`, \`github.com/go-jose/go-jose/v4\`, \`github.com/cpuguy83/go-md2man/v2\`, \`github.com/lmittmann/tint\`, \`github.com/oklog/ulid/v2\`.

## Test plan

- [x] \`mise run fmt && mise run lint && mise run test\` clean
- [x] \`entire labs\` lists all four new entries
- [x] \`entire repo --help\` shows the rebranded subcommand tree
- [x] \`entire org --help\`, \`entire project --help\`, \`entire grant --help\` ditto
- [x] \`entire project create\` (no args) prints \`project create\` usage + error
- [x] \`entire repo clone\` (no args) prints \`repo clone\` usage + error
- [x] \`entire foobarbaz\` still prints root usage + error (regression check)
- [x] \`entire --help\` does not list the hidden repo/org/project/grant commands
- [ ] End-to-end: \`entire login\` against a real cluster, then \`entire org list\` / \`entire repo list\` against entire-core (blocked on shipping the bridge to test users)

## Known follow-ups

- Refresh tokens aren't captured by device flow, so the vendored auto-refresh path logs a warning and falls back to the existing bearer on expiry. Same UX the cli has always had; proper refresh-token plumbing is a separate piece of work.
- Data-cluster discovery for the data-plane verbs (\`entire repo ls <cluster>/...\`) is still on the user — same as \`entire-core\`'s own model. There's no derivation from the JWT iss (the iss is the auth host, not the data cluster); upstream's mental model is "user knows their cluster" plus optional cluster_contexts pinning. Worth considering whether to bridge this too.
- The \`.golangci.yaml\` exclusion for \`internal/entiredb/\` is broad-brush so vendor refresh stays cheap; tightening it as we settle on the long-term tree is fine but not urgent.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -5

content.text:
This pivot makes a lot of sense — let me lay out what each API offers and what the architecture would look like.

## What's there

**Entire Core API** (`us.console.entire.io`, control plane):
- OpenAPI 3.1, bearer JWT or session cookie auth, RFC 7807 problem+json errors
- ~30 paths: `/orgs`, `/projects`, `/repos`, `/mirrors`, `/service-accounts`, `/audit`, `/me`, `/identity/handles/...`, `/access/*`, grants on each layer
- All clean unary JSON (request body → response body), no streaming
- Operation IDs are camelCase (`createOrg`, `listOrgs`, `grantProjectAccess`, `getRepo`, etc.) — codegen-friendly

**Entire Repo API** (`aws-us-east-2.entire.io`, per-cluster data plane):
- Same OpenAPI 3.1 + bearer JWT shape
- 17 paths under `/repos/{repoId}/*`: branches, commits, compare, files, merge-base, merges (+previews), rebases (+previews), reverts (+previews), tags, tree, plus `/repos/resolve` for owner/repo → repoId
- A handful (`diff`, `raw/{path...}`, `rebases`) have no response schema → streaming / raw bytes / NDJSON. Codegen will produce a method that hands back `*http.Response` for these; we'd unwrap them manually.

## Why this is a strong pivot

| | Vendor approach (current PR) | OpenAPI-first |
|---|---|---|
| LOC delta vs main | +11,384 | ~~+11K~~ → roughly +6–8K (generated client + CLI wrappers), and we replace, not add |
| New module deps | `grpc`, `connectrpc`, `caarlos0/env`, `go-jose`, `gofrs/flock`, `lmittmann/tint`, `oklog/ulid`, `cpuguy83/go-md2man` | likely just `oapi-codegen/runtime` (already pulled in by `gen/openapi/entiredb` last time) |
| Open-source story | Vendored from a private repo's main; refreshes track entiredb-internal Go | Generated from public OpenAPI specs at known URLs; nothing private crosses the boundary |
| Refresh strategy | `rsync -a entiredb/cmd/entire-*/cli → internal/entiredb/cmd/...` + manual surgery | `curl <spec> > internal/api/*.openapi.json && go generate ./...` |
| Streaming endpoints | Already-typed via vendored client | ~3–4 endpoints get hand-written wrappers (~200 LOC) |
| Cluster routing | Vendored cliauth + contexts.json + clidial | `/repos/{repoId}` on core returns the cluster URL → cli dials it directly. No contexts.json needed. |
| Auth | Bridge from `entire login` → contexts.json + entiredb keyring | `entire login`'s existing keyring slot, used directly as the bearer for both APIs (no STS bridge needed *if* the login JWT works against both — needs verifying) |

## Architecture I'd propose

```
internal/api/
├── specs/
│   ├── core.openapi.json        # ← curl-fetched from us.console.entire.io/api/v1/openapi.json
│   └── repo.openapi.json        # ← from aws-us-east-2.entire.io/api/v1/openapi.json
├── coreclient/
│   ├── gen.go                   # //go:generate oapi-codegen -package coreclient ...
│   └── client.go                # generated; ~3K LOC
├── repoclient/
│   ├── gen.go
│   ├── client.go                # generated; ~2K LOC
│   └── streaming.go             # hand-written for diff/raw/rebase events
└── auth/
    └── editor.go                # bearer-injecting RequestEditor that reads cli's auth.Store

cmd/entire/cli/
├── repo.go, org.go, project.go, grant.go    # CLI surface, calls into coreclient/repoclient
```

**Cluster routing without contexts.json**: when the user types `entire repo ls owner/widgets`, cli:
1. Calls core `/repos/by-mirror/...` or `/repos?...` to look up repo metadata, which includes the cluster URL.
2. Dials that cluster's repoclient.
No `<cluster>/et/<org>/<repo>` positional needed.

## Things I want to verify before we commit

content.text:
Yes — that simplifies things a lot, and I think it's the right call. Let me make sure I've got the split right.

## Which commands hit which API

Mapping the other PR's verbs to the two specs:

| Command | API | Keep if we drop Repo API? |
|---|---|---|
| `entire org` create/list | Core `/orgs` | ✅ keep |
| `entire project` create/list | Core `/projects`, `/orgs/{id}/projects` | ✅ keep |
| `entire grant` repo/project/org {add,remove,list} | Core `/…/grants`, `/orgs/{id}/members` | ✅ keep |
| `entire repo` **create / delete / list** | Core `/repos`, `/projects/{id}/repos` | ✅ keep |
| `entire repo` **mirror** | Core `/mirrors` | ✅ keep |
| `entire repo` clone / ls / log / diff / compare / branches / tags / merge / rebase / revert / get-file / merge-base | **Repo API** (`aws-us-east-2…`) | ❌ drop |

So dropping the Entire Repo API means the cli becomes a **control-plane client only**: org/project/grant/service-account management + repo *lifecycle* (create/delete/list) + mirror placement. The git content operations (clone, log, diff, server-side merge/rebase/revert) go away from this surface.

## Why that's a clean scope

- **One spec, one generated client** (`us.console.entire.io` Core API).
- **No streaming** — Core is all unary JSON. The hairy endpoints (diff/raw/rebase-events) were all on the Repo API; gone.
- **No cluster routing / per-cluster dialing / scoped-JWT exchange** — all of that machinery existed to reach data-plane clusters. Control plane is a single host.
- **Much smaller**: ~3K LOC generated + thin CLI wrappers, one dep (`oapi-codegen/runtime`).

## The one thing I want to confirm

`entire repo clone` is the interesting edge: cloning doesn't actually need the Repo *API* — it's just `git clone` over smart HTTP against the cluster's git endpoint, with the cli injecting the bearer. So it could survive even without the Repo API client.

53				}
54	
55				// Load settings once for telemetry and version check

66					agentStr := JoinAgentNames(installedAgents)
67					telemetry.TrackCommandDetached(cmd, agentStr, settings.Enabled, versioninfo.Version)
68				}
69	
70				// Version check and notification (synchronous with 2s timeout)
71				// Runs AFTER command completes to avoid interfering with interactive modes
72				versioncheck.CheckAndNotify(cmd.Context(), cmd.OutOrStdout(), versioninfo.Version)
73			},
74			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, _ []string) error {
75				ctx := cmd.Context()

77				if _, err := paths.WorktreeRoot(ctx); err == nil && !settings.IsSetUpAny(ctx) {

input.prompt: What does this library do — is it an OpenAPI code generator (produces a typed HTTP client/server), or a spec parsing/manipulation library? Does it support OpenAPI 3.1? Does it generate Go client code, or only parse/model/mutate/validate specs? Can it convert/downgrade 3.1 to 3.0? Summarize its actual purpose and primary use cases.

content.content:
# libopenapi: Purpose and Capabilities

**Primary Purpose:**
libopenapi is a "parser, library, validator and toolkit" rather than a code generator. It focuses on spec manipulation and analysis rather than generating typed clients or servers.

**OpenAPI Version Support:**
Yes, it supports OpenAPI 3.1 (plus 3.0, 3.2, Overlays, and Arazzo). The README states: "libopenapi has full support for OpenAPI 3, 3.1 and 3.2."

**Core Capabilities:**
- **Parsing & Modeling**: Reads and structures OpenAPI documents into Go data models
- **Validation**: Validates specifications against OpenAPI standards
- **Mutation**: Allows programmatic modification of spec documents
- **Diff/Analysis**: Includes a "What Changed" diff engine for comparing specs
- **Bundling**: Combines multiple spec files
- **Code Parsing**: Can extract API information from existing code

**Code Generation:**
The library includes a Go code generator (`generator/golang`), but documentation emphasizes it's for "Generating Code" from specs, not producing complete typed clients.

**Format Conversion:**
The documentation doesn't mention downgrading 3.1 to 3.0, suggesting this isn't a primary feature.

**Primary Use Cases:**
Validating specifications, analyzing API changes, bundling distributed specs, and building tools that operate on OpenAPI documents—not generating production-ready client SDKs.

input.prompt: Does ogen generate a typed Go HTTP client from an OpenAPI spec? What OpenAPI versions does it support — specifically does it support OpenAPI 3.1 and JSON Schema type-union nullability like `type: ["array","null"]`? List its key features and any stated limitations around 3.1 / nullable types.

content.content:
# Ogen: OpenAPI Code Generation for Go

**Typed Client Generation**
Yes, ogen generates statically typed Go HTTP clients. It provides "code-generated static radix router" and "Statically typed client and server" capabilities from OpenAPI specifications.

**OpenAPI Version Support**
The documentation explicitly states support for "OpenAPI v3" and mentions "JSON Schema draft 6" compatibility. However, **the content does not specify whether OpenAPI 3.1 or JSON Schema union types** (`type: ["array","null"]`) **are supported**. The schema examples shown use traditional nullable/optional field patterns rather than JSON Schema union syntax.

**Key Features:**
- No reflection or `interface{}` usage; JSON encoding is code-generated
- "No more boilerplate" — structures generated directly from specifications
- Generic wrappers (`Optional[T]`, `Nullable[T]`) instead of pointers for optional fields
- Sum types for `oneOf` with automatic discriminator inference
- Support for string formats (UUID, date-time, URI) as native Go types
- OpenTelemetry tracing and metrics
- Custom validation via `x-ogen-validate` extension

**Stated Limitations:**
The documentation notes that "If `ogen` encounters recursive types that can't be expressed in go, pointers are used as fallback." Beyond this, no explicit limitations regarding OpenAPI 3.1 or JSON Schema union-type nullability are documented.

content.text:
Researched both. They're not actually the same category — here's the honest comparison:

## libopenapi vs ogen

| | **ogen** | **libopenapi (pb33f)** |
|---|---|---|
| **Category** | Code generator | Spec parser / toolkit / validator |
| **Produces a typed HTTP client?** | ✅ Yes — typed methods, `Opt[T]`/`Nullable[T]` generics, sum types, no `interface{}` | ❌ No — parses/models/mutates/validates specs; its `generator/golang` is a model-codegen aid, not an SDK generator |
| **3.1 support** | Claims OpenAPI v3 + JSON Schema draft-6; **empirically v1.20.3 chokes on `type:["array","null"]`** (models `type` as a scalar) | ✅ Full 3.1 (it's the engine behind the `vacuum` linter) |
| **3.1 → 3.0 downgrade** | n/a | ❌ not a feature |
| **Fit for "first-class client to the endpoints"** | Direct fit | Wrong tool — you'd hand-write every HTTP call and use it only for parse/validate |

**Verdict: ogen is the better pick** — it's the only one of the two that actually generates the typed client we want. libopenapi is a spec-manipulation toolkit; choosing it would mean hand-rolling the client (the option you already declined) with libopenapi as a validation aid.

## The real blocker is orthogonal

Both ogen *and* oapi-codegen trip on the same thing: huma emits `type: ["array","null"]` (JSON Schema 2020-12 nullable shorthand) in 5 schemas. That's a spec-normalization problem, not a generator-choice problem. So the path is **ogen + a small normalization step** that rewrites those unions before generation.

Where libopenapi *could* legitimately earn a place is as that normalizer — load the 3.1 spec, mutate the type-unions, re-render — but a deterministic transform does the same job for 5 well-understood sites without adding a codegen-time dep.

No jq dependency, portable in CI, ~40 LOC. Refresh = curl spec + go generate.

options.label: ogen + libopenapi-based normalizer
options.description: Use libopenapi to load → mutate type-unions → re-render the spec, then ogen generates. More robust if the spec grows more 3.1-isms later, but adds libopenapi as a codegen-time dep for what is currently a 5-site transform.

options.label: ogen + commit a pre-normalized spec
options.description: Normalize once at fetch time (by hand/script), commit only the normalized spec. Simplest repo + generate step; the tradeoff is each spec refresh re-runs the normalization manually rather than via `go generate`.

cd /Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli; git add internal/coreapi go.mod go.sum && git commit -q -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
coreapi: generate a typed Core API client with ogen

Add a generated Go client for the Entire control-plane (Core) API —
the surface that manages orgs, projects, repos, mirrors, grants, and
service accounts. This is the OpenAPI-first alternative to vendoring
entiredb's CLI Go packages: nothing private crosses the boundary, the
client is regenerated from a public spec, and a refresh is a curl plus
`go generate`.

Pipeline (internal/coreapi/gen.go):

  1. spec/core.openapi.json — the pristine upstream spec, fetched
     verbatim from <core-host>/api/v1/openapi.json.
  2. spec/normalize.go — rewrites it into spec/core.gen.json:
       - collapses huma's JSON-Schema-2020-12 nullable shorthand
         (`type: ["array","null"]` → `"array"`), which ogen's scalar
         `type` model rejects, matching the server's move to
         non-nullable arrays (absent ⇒ `[]`, never null);
       - replaces each operation's explicit 4xx/5xx responses (all of
         which already reference the same ErrorModel) with a single
         `default` error response, so ogen emits convenient errors —
         operations return `(*T, error)` with non-2xx surfacing as a
         typed `*ErrorModelStatusCode` — instead of a per-operation
         response sum type that forces a type switch at every call site.
  3. ogen (ogen.yml) — generates client-only (server / webhooks /
     unimplemented / otel features disabled), 24k LOC of typed models +
     client across the oas_*.go files.

client.go is the hand-written surface:
  - New() dials <auth-host>/api/v1 (the login host is the control-plane
    host; ENTIRE_AUTH_BASE_URL overrides) and authenticates with the
    logged-in bearer, resolved lazily per request via
    auth.TokenForResource so an RFC 8693 exchange happens transparently
    when the stored token's audience doesn't cover the control plane.
  - APIError(err) extracts the RFC 7807 problem detail/title for a clean
    user-facing message; covered by client_test.go.

New module deps are the ogen runtime family (go-faster/jx, go-faster/errors,
ogen-go/ogen runtime packages) pulled in by the generated code.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)" && echo "committed coreapi"; git log --oneline -1
